stt.stt_text:
As campaigns go, the one in 1892 was not a particularly
 exciting one.
 Both candidates had already served a term in the White
 House.
 Cleveland from 1884 to 1888, Harrison succeeding him and
 running now for re-election.
 Both men were well known to the voters.
 It was a time of industrial expansion for the nation, and
 there were no earth-shaking issues at stake,
 save that of governmental spending, which even in a
 prosperous year made many voters dissatisfied with the
 Harrison administration.
 Cleveland sat out the campaign at his home in Buzzards Bay,
 suffering from the gout and making an occasional speech.
 Harrison, whose wife had just died, stayed in the White
 House.
